literature.headline_zh: 尼帕病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期尼帕病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 我们采用多重免疫组织化学技术来分析在母体和胎儿胎盘细胞中鉴定出 NiV 抗原的特定细胞群,这在 NiV 疾病的非人灵长类动物模型中之前尚未被描述过。 [10.1093/infdis/jiag321]
研究发现,T 淋巴细胞在控制 NiV 感染中发挥着关键作用,而 B 淋巴细胞和 NK 细胞则不是必需的。吞噬细胞(特别是 CD169 + 巨噬细胞)的消耗增加了对 NiV 感染的易感性。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2763840]
通过对 FDA 批准的药物进行虚拟筛选并结合整体对接,我们确定考尼伐坦是 尼帕病毒 基质蛋白的潜在抑制剂。 [10.1039/d6cp02765b]
与 NiV-Bangladesh 相比,NiV-Malaysia 导致仓鼠死亡率增加、呼吸窘迫和神经系统疾病,并且大脑和肺部出现更严重的病变和病毒信号。 [10.3390/v18111263]
该评论强调,基于 miRNA 的 尼帕病毒 诊断的临床采用将取决于将这些特征集成到经济实惠的样本到答案平台中,并证明结果可以改善现实条件下确定的临床决策。 [10.1080/14737159.2026.2763735]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: We employed multiplex immunohistochemistry techniques to profile specific cell populations that identified NiV antigen in both maternal and fetal cells of the placenta, which has not been previously described in nonhuman primate models of NiV disease. [10.1093/infdis/jiag321]

T lymphocytes were found to play a critical role in controlling NiV infection, while B lymphocytes and NK cells were not essential. Depletion of phagocytes, specifically CD169 + macrophages, increased susceptibility to NiV infection. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2763840]
Using virtual screening of FDA-approved drugs combined with ensemble docking, we identified conivaptan as a potential inhibitor of the Nipah virus matrix protein. [10.1039/d6cp02765b]

NiV-Malaysia caused increased lethality, respiratory distress, and neurological disease in hamsters, along with more severe pathologies and viral signals in both the brain and lungs compared to NiV-Bangladesh. [10.3390/v18111263]

The review highlights that clinical adoption of miRNA-based diagnostics for Nipah virus will depend on integrating these signatures into affordable sample-to-answer platforms and demonstrating that results improve defined clinical decisions under real-world conditions. [10.1080/14737159.2026.2763735]

news.headline_zh: 尼帕病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期尼帕病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: LSHTM 研究人员对印度和孟加拉国的 尼帕病毒 暴发 进行了历史分析,得出结论,有针对性的遏制策略是预防 暴发 的最有效方法。 [news-cce683325d57d4c1]
《公共卫生前沿》发表的一篇综合科学评论评估了妊娠期间 尼帕病毒 感染对母体、胎儿和管理的挑战。它强调,虽然实验动物研究表明该病毒可以穿过胎盘屏障,但已证实的人类垂直 传播 仍未得到证实。 [news-4ba2266d984994c9]
一项系统回顾和建模研究评估了孟加拉国和印度的 尼帕病毒 传播 动态,表明该病毒以自限性方式传播,但高度过度分散。研究结果基于 暴发 的历史数据,并得到了作者的证实。 [news-c5ffb7162524f44f]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Nipah virus news developments.
key_findings_en: LSHTM researchers conducted a historical analysis of Nipah virus outbreaks in India and Bangladesh, concluding that targeted containment strategies are the most effective for preventing outbreaks. [news-cce683325d57d4c1]
A comprehensive scientific review published in Frontiers in Public Health evaluates the maternal, fetal, and management challenges of Nipah virus infection during pregnancy. [news-4ba2266d984994c9]

A systematic review and modeling study evaluated Nipah virus transmission dynamics in Bangladesh and India, revealing that the virus spreads in a self-limiting manner but is highly overdispersed. The findings are based on data from historical outbreaks and are confirmed by the authors. [news-c5ffb7162524f44f]
news.trend_or_risk_en: Risk statements are limited to information confirmed by eligible sources and do not upgrade media speculation into official conclusions.

papers.title: Immune control of lethal Nipah virus infection: the critical role of host macrophages
papers.abstract: Abstract Nipah virus (NiV) is highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxovirus of Henipaviru s genus that causes recurrent human outbreaks in South-East Asia, with a lethality of 40-75%. Immunopathogenesis associated to this emerging virus is still poorly understood and the role of different components of the immune response in the control of infection remains unknown. In contrast to many other mammalian species, wild type mice are resistant to NiV infection, due to an efficient type-I interferon response. We have analysed the role of various immune cell populations in the control of NiV infection and demonstrated the critical role of T lymphocytes but neither B lymphocytes nor NK cells were primordial. In addition, the depletion of phagocytes in mice by injection of clodronate liposomes resulted in dramatical increase of their susceptibility to NiV infection. Moreover, using CD169-DTR transgenic mice we show here that the specific depletion of CD169 + macrophages results in an increased susceptibility of mice to NiV challenge, highlighting the important role of this cell population. Finally, in NiV-infected African green monkeys, which closely resemble severe human Nipah disease, the production of virus-induced type-I and -II interferons was followed with an important increase of CD169 + cells in the blood and lungs, with some of them being NiV-infected. As CD169 + macrophages have been described to play an important role at the crossroads between innate and adaptive immunity in various infections, these results reveal their potentially determining role during NiV infection as well, which may help to better understand this highly lethal infectious disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the role of different immune cell populations in controlling Nipah virus (NiV) infection, given the poor understanding of the immunopathogenesis of this highly pathogenic zoonotic virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used wild type mice and CD169-DTR transgenic mice to investigate the role of various immune cell populations in NiV infection, with African green monkeys serving as a model for severe human Nipah disease.
analysis.methods: The researchers analyzed the role of T lymphocytes, B lymphocytes, NK cells, and macrophages in NiV infection using depletion experiments and transgenic mice.
analysis.main_results: T lymphocytes were found to play a critical role in controlling NiV infection, while B lymphocytes and NK cells were not essential. Depletion of phagocytes, specifically CD169 + macrophages, increased susceptibility to NiV infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the critical role of CD169 + macrophages in controlling NiV infection, which may help in understanding the immunopathogenesis of this highly lethal disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting CD169 + macrophages could be a potential therapeutic strategy for NiV infection, and may aid in the development of better diagnostic tools and preventive measures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of mice as a model, which may not fully represent human disease. The findings in mice need to be validated in human studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of various immune cell populations in controlling Nipah virus infection using mice and transgenic models. It demonstrated the critical role of T lymphocytes and the importance of CD169 + macrophages in controlling NiV infection, highlighting potential therapeutic and diagnostic strategies.

papers.title_zh: 致死性 尼帕病毒 感染的免疫控制:宿主 巨噬细胞的关键作用
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Nipah virus (NiV) is highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxovirus of Henipaviru s genus that causes recurrent human outbreaks in South-East Asia, with a lethality of 40-75%. Immunopathogenesis associated to this emerging virus is still poorly understood and the role of different components of the immune response in the control of infection remains unknown. In contrast to many other mammalian species, wild type mice are resistant to NiV infection, due to an efficient type-I interferon response. We have analysed the role of various immune cell populations in the control of NiV infection and demonstrated the critical role of T lymphocytes but neither B lymphocytes nor NK cells were primordial. In addition, the depletion of phagocytes in mice by injection of clodronate liposomes resulted in dramatical increase of their susceptibility to NiV infection. Moreover, using CD169-DTR transgenic mice we show here that the specific depletion of CD169 + macrophages results in an increased susceptibility of mice to NiV challenge, highlighting the important role of this cell population. Finally, in NiV-infected African green monkeys, which closely resemble severe human Nipah disease, the production of virus-induced type-I and -II interferons was followed with an important increase of CD169 + cells in the blood and lungs, with some of them being NiV-infected. As CD169 + macrophages have been described to play an important role at the crossroads between innate and adaptive immunity in various infections, these results reveal their potentially determining role during NiV infection as well, which may help to better understand this highly lethal infectious disease.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 是亨尼帕病毒属高致病性人畜共患副粘病毒,在东南亚引起人类 暴发 复发,致死率为 40-75%。与这种新兴病毒相关的免疫发病机制仍然知之甚少,免疫应答 的不同成分在控制感染中的作用仍然未知。与许多其他哺乳动物物种相比,野生型小鼠由于有效的 I 型干扰素反应而对 NiV 感染具有抵抗力。我们分析了各种免疫细胞群在控制 NiV 感染中的作用,并证明了 T 淋巴细胞的关键作用,但 B 淋巴细胞和 NK 细胞都不是原始细胞。此外,通过注射氯膦酸盐脂质体来消耗小鼠体内的吞噬细胞导致其对NiV感染的易感性急剧增加。此外,使用 CD169-DTR 转基因小鼠,我们在此表明​​ CD169 + 巨噬细胞的特异性消耗导致小鼠对 NiV 攻击的敏感性增加,突出了该细胞群的重要作用。最后,在感染 NiV 的非洲绿猴中(与严重的人类尼帕病非常相似),病毒诱导的 I 型和 II 型干扰素产生,随后血液和肺部的 CD169 + 细胞显着增加,其中一些被 NiV 感染。由于 CD169 + 巨噬细胞已被描述在各种感染中先天性免疫和适应性免疫之间的十字路口发挥着重要作用,因此这些结果也揭示了它们在 NiV 感染期间的潜在决定作用,这可能有助于更好地了解这种高度致命的传染病。

papers.title: Deterministic–stochastic fractional-order modeling and optimal control of Nipah virus in hypertensive nephrosclerosis
papers.abstract: Nipah virus is a zoonotic virus that causes severe respiratory and neurological disease and is spread through pigs, bats or contaminated food. This research develops a fractional-order mathematical model to investigate the co-infection dynamics of hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus infection. The model is kept positive and bounded to guarantee biological reality, and the disease-free equilibrium E p l is studied. The basic reproduction number R 0 l p < 1 implies extinction of the infection while R 0 l p > 1 implies small outbreaks developing into epidemics. These results are backed up by bifurcation analysis, global stability analysis and existence and uniqueness proofs for the solution. Real Malaysian co-infection data was used to parameterise the model, and simulations were carried out for both deterministic and stochastic fractional systems. The fractional-order parameter has significant impact on the infection rates and convergence behaviour. The memory effects and nonlocal dynamics are described by using piecewise Caputo–Fabrizio derivatives. Stochastic perturbations are considered to model random environmental effects. The parameters were changed to highlight the role of vaccination and stochasticity in disease extinction. The amalgamation of Caputo–Fabrizio fractional calculus and stochastic modelling, supported by a novel numerical scheme, offers a robust and flexible approach to simulate co-infection dynamics under uncertainty. The framework is further validated by PRCC sensitivity analysis and MCMC parameter estimation. Optimal control strategies provide to control the co-infection spread with economic feasibility. To summarize, the model provides useful insights into the interaction between hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus transmission, supporting the design of effective and economically feasible control strategies.

papers.title: Competitive inhibition of the Nipah virus matrix protein by conivaptan: from binding pocket dynamics to protein–membrane interactions
papers.abstract: The recurrent outbreaks of Nipah virus since its first emergence have intensified efforts to identify effective antiviral therapeutics. The matrix protein is a key structural protein that maintains virion architecture and plays a crucial role in anchoring the virus to the host plasma membrane. Binding of phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) to the matrix protein promotes conformational changes that facilitate membrane association and initiate viral assembly. Therefore, an effective small-molecule inhibitor should not only compete with PIP2 for binding to the Nipah virus matrix protein (NiVM) but also disrupt its interaction with the host membrane. Using virtual screening of FDA-approved drugs combined with ensemble docking, we identified conivaptan as a potential inhibitor of the Nipah virus matrix protein. The multivalent interactions of conivaptan establish stable binding within the PIP2-binding pocket while simultaneously rewiring protein-membrane interactions. In the presence of PIP2, NiVM anchors to the membrane through multiple charged residues, resulting in pronounced local bilayer deformation, an early signature of membrane remodeling. In contrast, conivaptan binding weakens membrane anchoring and preserves a more ordered and compact bilayer, thereby suppressing membrane deformation. Together, these findings identify conivaptan as a promising repurposable inhibitor of the Nipah virus matrix protein and provide a mechanistic framework for targeting virus-membrane interactions during viral assembly.

papers.source_body_en: The recurrent outbreaks of Nipah virus since its first emergence have intensified efforts to identify effective antiviral therapeutics. The matrix protein is a key structural protein that maintains virion architecture and plays a crucial role in anchoring the virus to the host plasma membrane. Binding of phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) to the matrix protein promotes conformational changes that facilitate membrane association and initiate viral assembly. papers.abstract_zh: 自 尼帕病毒 首次出现以来,暴发 的反复出现加大了寻找有效 抗病毒药物 疗法的努力。基质蛋白是维持病毒颗粒结构的关键结构蛋白,在将病毒锚定到 宿主 质膜上起着至关重要的作用。4,5-二磷酸磷脂酰肌醇 (PIP2) 与基质蛋白的结合可促进构象变化,从而促进膜结合并启动病毒组装。因此,有效的小分子抑制剂不仅应与 PIP2 竞争与 尼帕病毒 基质蛋白 (NiVM) 的结合,而且还应破坏其与 宿主 膜的相互作用。通过对 FDA 批准的药物进行虚拟筛选并结合整体对接,我们确定考尼伐坦是 尼帕病毒 基质蛋白的潜在抑制剂。conivaptan 的多价相互作用在 PIP2 结合袋内建立稳定的结合,同时重新连接蛋白质-膜相互作用。在 PIP2 存在的情况下,NiVM 通过多个带电残基锚定在膜上,导致明显的局部双层变形,这是膜重塑的早期特征。相反,考尼伐坦结合削弱了膜锚定并保留了更有序和致密的双层,从而抑制了膜变形。总之,这些发现表明考尼伐坦是一种有前途的 尼帕病毒 基质蛋白的可重复利用抑制剂,并为病毒组装过程中靶向病毒-膜相互作用提供了机制框架。

papers.title: Vertical Transmission of Nipah Virus in an Experimentally Infected Nonhuman Primate: A Brief Report and Description of Histopathological Lesions.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic henipavirus that causes severe, often fatal disease in humans and animals. African green monkeys have been used extensively to investigate NiV disease and are the only nonhuman primate model that accurately recapitulates human NiV pathogenesis. Here, we describe histopathological lesions in the reproductive tissues of an incidentally pregnant female African green monkey that succumbed to NiV disease. We employed multiplex immunohistochemistry techniques to profile specific cell populations that identified NiV antigen in both maternal and fetal cells of the placenta, which has not been previously described in nonhuman primate models of NiV disease.

papers.title: Characterization of Nipah Virus Strains Malaysia and Bangladesh in a Hamster Aerosol-Exposure Model
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is an enveloped, single-stranded, negative-sense virus that causes severe respiratory distress and neurological disease in humans. While NiV disease is associated with high mortality rates (40–70%), no FDA-approved medical countermeasures (MCM) against NiV currently exist. Phylogenetic analyses have clustered isolates from Malaysia (NiV-M) and Bangladesh (NiV-B) into two distinct circulating strains associated with unique transmission routes, clinical manifestations, and lethality rates in humans. Predominantly spread by zoonotic transmission, NiV-M yields lower case-fatality rates, mild respiratory symptoms, and severe neurological manifestations. In contrast, NiV-B showcases higher case-fatality rates, marked respiratory disease, and human-to-human transmission via respiratory secretions. NiV hamster models utilizing aerosol, oronasal, intranasal, intracranial, and intraperitoneal inoculations exist. However, aerosol infection of NiV-B in hamsters remains poorly understood, while direct strain comparisons using aerosolization as an inoculation route have yet to be performed. To establish a Syrian golden hamster model comparing NiV strain-specific disease presentations and pathologies following aerosol exposure for downstream MCM characterization, we infected SGHs with a range of NiV-M and NiV-B aerosol inocula, determined the median lethal dose (LD50) and survival curves, and further elucidated both histopathological changes and viral antigen distribution within the brain and lungs. We found increased NiV-M lethality, respiratory distress, and neurological disease, in addition to more severe pathologies and viral signal within both the brain and lungs compared to NiV-B-infected animals. Our study serves as the first to compare aerosol exposure of NiV-B versus NiV-M in a hamster model, which can subsequently be used for crucial strain-specific MCM characterizations.

While NiV disease is associated with high mortality rates (40–70%), no FDA-approved medical countermeasures (MCM) against NiV currently exist. Phylogenetic analyses have clustered isolates from Malaysia (NiV-M) and Bangladesh (NiV-B) into two distinct circulating strains associated with unique transmission routes, clinical manifestations, and lethality rates in humans. Predominantly spread by zoonotic transmission, NiV-M yields lower case-fatality rates, mild respiratory symptoms, and severe neurological manifestations. In contrast, NiV-B showcases higher case-fatality rates, marked respiratory disease, and human-to-human transmission via respiratory secretions. NiV hamster models utilizing aerosol, oronasal, intranasal, intracranial, and intraperitoneal inoculations exist. However, aerosol infection of NiV-B in hamsters remains poorly understood, while direct strain comparisons using aerosolization as an inoculation route have yet to be performed. To establish a Syrian golden hamster model comparing NiV strain-specific disease presentations and pathologies following aerosol exposure for downstream MCM characterization, we infected SGHs with a range of NiV-M and NiV-B aerosol inocula, determined the median lethal dose (LD50) and survival curves, and further elucidated both histopathological changes and viral antigen distribution within the brain and lungs. We found increased NiV-M lethality, respiratory distress, and neurological disease, in addition to more severe pathologies and viral signal within both the brain and lungs compared to NiV-B-infected animals. Our study serves as the first to compare aerosol exposure of NiV-B versus NiV-M in a hamster model, which can subsequently be used for crucial strain-specific MCM characterizations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus (NiV) causes severe respiratory distress and neurological disease in humans, with high mortality rates and no FDA-approved medical countermeasures (MCM) currently available. The study aimed to characterize NiV strains from Malaysia and Bangladesh in a hamster aerosol-exposure model to support downstream MCM development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized a Syrian golden hamster model to compare NiV-Malaysia and NiV-Bangladesh strains following aerosol exposure. The research was conducted in 2026 and involved infecting hamsters with varying aerosol inocula to determine median lethal doses and survival curves.
analysis.methods: The researchers infected Syrian golden hamsters with aerosolized NiV-M and NiV-B strains, measured lethality and disease symptoms, and analyzed histopathological changes and viral antigen distribution in the brain and lungs using standardized protocols.
analysis.main_results: NiV-Malaysia caused increased lethality, respiratory distress, and neurological disease in hamsters, along with more severe pathologies and viral signals in both the brain and lungs compared to NiV-Bangladesh.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight strain-specific differences in disease presentation and pathogenesis following aerosol exposure, providing critical insights for the development of strain-specific medical countermeasures.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform the design of targeted surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for NiV-Malaysia and NiV-Bangladesh, particularly in aerosol transmission scenarios.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a hamster model, which may not fully represent human disease. However, the evidence is strong as it directly compares aerosol-exposed NiV strains in a relevant animal model.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized Nipah virus (NiV) strains from Malaysia and Bangladesh in a Syrian golden hamster aerosol-exposure model. NiV-Malaysia was found to cause higher lethality, respiratory distress, and neurological disease compared to NiV-Bangladesh, with more severe pathologies and viral signals in both the brain and lungs. The research provides critical insights into strain-specific disease presentations, supporting the development of targeted medical countermeasures. The study is limited to an animal model, but the evidence is strong due to direct comparisons of aerosol-exposed strains. These findings have implications for understanding NiV transmission and improving surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for both strains.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 会导致人类严重呼吸窘迫和神经系统疾病,死亡率 发生率较高,且目前尚无 FDA 批准的医疗对策 (MCM)。该研究旨在通过仓鼠气溶胶暴露模型来表征来自马来西亚和孟加拉国的 NiV 毒株,以支持下游 MCM 的开发。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用叙利亚金仓鼠模型来比较气溶胶暴露后的 NiV-Malaysia 和 NiV-Bangladesh 菌株。该研究于 2026 年进行,涉及用不同的气溶胶接种物感染仓鼠,以确定中位致死剂量和生存曲线。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员用雾化的 NiV-M 和 NiV-B 菌株感染叙利亚金仓鼠,测量致死率和疾病症状,并使用标准化方案分析组织病理学变化和病毒抗原在大脑和肺部的分布。
elements_zh.main_results: 与 NiV-Bangladesh 相比,NiV-Malaysia 导致仓鼠死亡率增加、呼吸窘迫和神经系统疾病,并且大脑和肺部出现更严重的病变和病毒信号。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了气溶胶暴露后疾病表现和 发病机制 的菌株特异性差异,为制定菌株特异性医疗对策提供了重要见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果可以为 NiV-马来西亚和 NiV-孟加拉国设计有针对性的 监测、诊断 和 治疗 策略提供信息,特别是在气溶胶 传播 场景中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于仓鼠模型,可能无法完全代表人类疾病。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它直接比较了相关动物模型中暴露于气溶胶​​的 NiV 菌株。

papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 是一种有包膜、单链、负义病毒,可导致人类严重呼吸窘迫和神经系统疾病。虽然 NiV 疾病与高 死亡率 发生率 (40-70%) 相关,但目前尚无 FDA 批准的针对 NiV 的医疗对策 (MCM)。系统发育分析将来自马来西亚 (NiV-M) 和孟加拉国 (NiV-B) 的分离株聚类为两种不同的流行毒株,这两种毒株与独特的 传播 途径、临床表现和人类致死率相关。NiV-M 主要通过人畜共患 传播 传播,病死率较低,呼吸道症状轻微,神经系统症状严重。相比之下,NiV-B 表现出较高的病死率、明显的呼吸道疾病以及通过呼吸道分泌物进行人际传播的 传播。存在利用气雾剂、口鼻、鼻内、颅内和腹膜内接种的 NiV 仓鼠模型。然而,对仓鼠中 NiV-B 气溶胶感染的了解仍知之甚少,而使用气溶胶作为接种途径的直接菌株比较尚未进行。为了建立叙利亚金仓鼠模型,比较气溶胶暴露后的 NiV 毒株特异性疾病表现和病理,以进行下游 MCM 表征,我们用一系列 NiV-M 和 NiV-B 气溶胶接种物感染 SGH,确定中位致死剂量 (LD50) 和生存曲线,并进一步阐明脑和肺内的组织病理学变化和病毒抗原分布。我们发现,与感染 NiV-B 的动物相比,NiV-M 的致死率、呼吸窘迫和神经系统疾病有所增加,此外,大脑和肺部的病理和病毒信号也更严重。我们的研究首次在仓鼠模型中比较了 NiV-B 与 NiV-M 的气​​溶胶暴露,随后可用于关键的菌株特异性 MCM 表征。

papers.title: MicroRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases: from biomarker discovery to clinical implementation
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are increasingly investigated as host-response biomarkers for infectious diseases, but translation from differential-expression studies to clinically deployable diagnostics remains limited. AREAS COVERED: This review evaluates the diagnostic and translational potential of miRNAs across malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika virus infection, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nipah virus disease. papers.title: Cas13d-mediated viral RNA degradation leads to potent antiviral control against both positive and negative sense RNA viruses
papers.abstract: Respiratory viral infections continue to pose a substantial global health challenge, with a pressing need for effective treatment options. The rapid mutation rate of RNA viruses presents a significant risk of escape from existing treatments. Here, we harness the rapid adaptability and high sequence specificity of the RNA-targeting CRISPR-Cas13 nuclease technology to target and cleave the genome of different RNA viruses, disrupting replication and impairing propagation. We identified potent CRISPR-RfxCas13d/crRNA (Cas13d/crRNA) combinations that can efficiently restrict viral replication in both pre- and post-viral exposure treatment settings. In vitro treatment with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) co-encapsulating Cas13d mRNA and crRNAs targeting coding and non-coding regions of positive-sense (+) RNA coronaviruses including SARS-CoV-2 effectively inhibited viral replication. In addition, both pre- and post-viral exposure treatments with the LNP-Cas13d/crRNA against the negative-sense (−) RNA Nipah virus resulted in 99% restriction of this highly pathogenic virus. Hence, the Cas13d/crRNA antiviral method holds promise as a potential therapeutic approach against severe viral infections caused by both (+) and (−) RNA viruses. Furthermore, the multi-locus targeting of viruses by Cas13d could offer a possibility to prevent virus breakthrough and increase the therapeutic arsenal against many emerging RNA viruses in the future.

source_records.title: Cas13d-mediated viral RNA degradation leads to potent antiviral control against both positive and negative sense RNA viruses
source_records.abstract: Respiratory viral infections continue to pose a substantial global health challenge, with a pressing need for effective treatment options. The rapid mutation rate of RNA viruses presents a significant risk of escape from existing treatments. Here, we harness the rapid adaptability and high sequence specificity of the RNA-targeting CRISPR-Cas13 nuclease technology to target and cleave the genome of different RNA viruses, disrupting replication and impairing propagation. We identified potent CRISPR-RfxCas13d/crRNA (Cas13d/crRNA) combinations that can efficiently restrict viral replication in both pre- and post-viral exposure treatment settings. Hence, the Cas13d/crRNA antiviral method holds promise as a potential therapeutic approach against severe viral infections caused by both (+) and (−) RNA viruses. papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道病毒感染继续对全球健康构成重大挑战,迫切需要有效的 治疗 方案。RNA病毒的快速突变速率带来了从现有突变逃逸的重大风险。在这里,我们利用RNA靶向CRISPR-Cas13核酸酶技术的快速适应性和高序列特异性来靶向和切割不同RNA病毒的基因组,破坏复制并损害繁殖。我们发现了有效的 CRISPR-RfxCas13d/crRNA (Cas13d/crRNA) 组合,可以在病毒暴露前和病毒暴露后 治疗 设置中有效限制病毒复制。体外 治疗 与脂质纳米颗粒 (LNP) 共封装 Cas13d mRNA 和 crRNA,靶向正义 (+) RNA 冠状病毒(包括 SARS-CoV-2)的编码和非编码区域,可有效抑制病毒复制。此外,病毒暴露前和病毒后 治疗 与针对负义 (-) RNA 尼帕病毒 的 LNP-Cas13d/crRNA 均导致对这种高致病性病毒的 99% 限制。因此,Cas13d/crRNA 抗病毒药物 方法有望成为针对 (+) 和 (-) RNA 病毒引起的严重病毒感染的潜在治疗方法。此外,Cas13d 对病毒的多位点靶向可以提供防止病毒突破的可能性,并增加未来针对许多新兴 RNA 病毒的治疗手段。

events News Targeted containment best way to stop outbreaks of Nipah virus Targeted containment best way to stop outbreaks of Nipah virus 16 November 2026 London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine https://lshtm.ac.uk/themes/custom/lshtm/images/lshtm-logo-black.png Share Analysis of historical outbreaks in India and Bangladesh found uneven spread of Nipah virus, showing targeted containment as best way to tackle outbreaks. Targeted strategies of containment are the best approach to protect against outbreaks of Nipah virus, according to new modelling research from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM). A historical analysis of outbreaks in India and Bangladesh showed that most Nipah virus outbreaks die out with low transmissibility. However, some cases can develop into dangerous outbreaks. In such cases, the researchers argue that targeted quarantines and contact tracing are the best approach for containment. The findings could also inform other public health initiatives against future Nipah virus outbreaks as well as the drive to develop new vaccines. Published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases, the researchers collected reports of Nipah virus outbreaks from 2001 to 2026 in Bangladesh and India, and modelled these data to understand how the virus spreads. It is the first analysis of Nipah virus’ spread, compiling all known outbreaks in India. Nipah virus was first identified in 1998 in an outbreak among pig farms in Maylasia, with the virus spreading only from animals to humans. After its initial outbreak in South East Asia, Nipah virus spread to India and Bangladesh in 2001 where outbreaks have been reported almost every year since. These findings are timely, as Nipah virus has been classified a ‘priority disease’ by the World Health Organization (WHO) due to its potential to develop into an epidemic. This calls for more research and development to improve our understanding of the virus, developing tests, and treatments against Nipah virus like vaccines. The variants of Nipah virus in India and Bangladesh are unique, as they are the only versions identified so far that can be spread directly between humans. Studying these variants are vital to understand how Nipah virus could develop into, and public health strategies to prevent, a future pandemic. As a disease that has recently emerged, there is less research on Nipah virus. Sol Kim, PhD student and lead author at LSHTM, said: "Our work analyses the historical Nipah outbreaks in Bangladesh and India to measure how many people each patient infects, how unevenly that spread is shared, and how quickly new cases follow. This work is part of our efforts on epidemic and pandemic preparedness against Nipah virus, which is considered a high-priority pathogen in public health.” The model’s results found that it takes, on average, 13 days for the virus to pass from one person to another.. However, Nipah virus spreads unevenly, meaning that most people with an infection will be unlikely to spread it to other people. But a small proportion of those infected will unwittingly act as ‘super-spreaders’ to others, and drive most of the growth in Nipah virus infections during an outbreak. This fact is very important in guiding public health efforts about Nipah virus outbreaks to control its spread. As infections spread unevenly in specific cases of high clusters, the authors recommend targeted measures such as contact tracing for affected areas and quarantines specific to affected families or neighbourhoods, rather than blanket approaches like lockdown quarantines. Alongside containment, these findings could support the development of new vaccines. The uneven dispersion will need to be considered when designing clinical trials for Nipah virus vaccine candidates, and the best strategy for delivering vaccines during a potential epidemic. Such studies are needed because they provide baseline numbers that can be used to monitor the virus and inform further modelling studies by updating what we know. Publication Sol Kim et al. Transmission dynamics of Nipah virus in Bangladesh and India, 2001-2026: Systematic review and inference on reproduction number, offspring dispersion, and serial interval. PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases. analysis.brief_en: A new study by the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) highlights that targeted containment strategies are the most effective way to stop Nipah virus outbreaks. news.title_zh: 针对性遏制暴发的尼帕病毒的最佳方式 - LSHTM
news.source_body_en: A new study by the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) highlights that targeted containment strategies are the most effective way to stop Nipah virus outbreaks. The research, published on 2026-11-16, analyzed historical outbreaks in India and Bangladesh from 2001 to 2026. It found that while most outbreaks die out due to the virus's low transmissibility, some cases can escalate into dangerous outbreaks. The virus spreads unevenly, with a small proportion of infected individuals acting as super-spreaders. Based on these findings, the researchers recommend targeted quarantines and contact tracing for affected areas, rather than broad lockdown measures. The study also emphasizes the need for further research and vaccine development to address the virus's potential for future epidemics. This work contributes to epidemic preparedness and provides baseline data for monitoring and modeling Nipah virus spread.
news.content_zh: 伦敦卫生与热带医学院 (LSHTM) 的一项新研究强调,有针对性的遏制策略是阻止 尼帕病毒 暴发 的最有效方法。该研究发表于2026年11月16日,分析了2001年至2026年印度和孟加拉国的历史暴发。研究发现,虽然大多数暴发由于病毒的低传播性而死亡,但某些病例可能会升级为危险的暴发。该病毒传播不均匀,一小部分感染者充当超级传播者。根据这些发现,研究人员建议对受影响地区进行有针对性的隔离和接触者追踪,而不是广泛的封锁措施。该研究还强调需要进一步研究和 疫苗 开发,以解决该病毒未来流行病的可能性。这项工作有助于流行病防范,并为监测和建模 尼帕病毒 传播提供基线数据。

Classified by the World Health Organization as an urgent priority pathogen due to case fatality rates spanning between 40 percent and 90 percent, Nipah virus is an enveloped, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA paramyxovirus within the genus Henipavirus. The pathogen was initially identified during the 1998 to 1999 outbreak across Malaysia and Singapore and has since triggered recurrent, near-annual outbreaks concentrated primarily in Bangladesh and India. Although human-to-human transmission occurs through direct contact with contaminated bodily fluids or respiratory droplets, the primary zoonotic pathway involves spillover from pteropod fruit bats, specifically Pteropus medius, through the consumption of raw date palm sap or contaminated fruits. The synthesized findings emphasize that while experimental animal inoculations demonstrate that the virus can breach the placental barrier and infect fetal organs, confirmed vertical transmission in human clinical cases has not yet been virologically established. The structural and genomic architecture of Nipah virus underpins its widespread tissue tropism and severe clinical pathogenicity across mammalian hosts. Spanning approximately 18.2 kilobases, the viral genome encodes six structural proteins: the nucleocapsid, phosphoprotein, matrix protein, fusion glycoprotein, attachment glycoprotein, and large polymerase. Infection initiates when the viral attachment glycoprotein binds host ephrin-B2 or ephrin-B3 cell surface receptors, which triggers fusion glycoprotein-mediated membrane entry into target cells. Because ephrin-B2 and ephrin-B3 receptors are extensively expressed across arterial endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells, neurons, and respiratory epithelium, the virus displays profound systemic tropism. Initial viral replication occurs in the epithelial cells of the respiratory tract following mucosal exposure, after which the pathogen disseminates into vascular endothelial cells. This process stimulates syncytium formation, severe endothelial inflammation, and extensive vasculitis. Disruption of the vascular endothelial layer permits entry into the bloodstream, where the virus circulates either freely or bound to leukocytes, resulting in widespread multi-organ dissemination involving the lungs, brain, heart, spleen, and kidneys. Clinical manifestations of Nipah virus infection vary from asymptomatic infection to rapidly progressive, fulminant central nervous system pathology and acute respiratory distress syndrome. Following an incubation interval typically lasting 4 to 14 days, though occasionally extending up to 45 days or beyond, patients present with non-specific prodromal features including high fever, headache, myalgia, vomiting, sore throat, and respiratory complaints. In severe clinical courses, infection rapidly advances to marked neurological dysfunction characterized by dizziness, drowsiness, altered mental status, myoclonus, hyperreflexia or areflexia, convulsions, and terminal coma. Histopathological investigations in fatal cases reveal widespread systemic vasculitis, focal thrombosis, and extensive parenchymal necrosis, with viral antigen concentrated within cerebral, renal, and pulmonary tissues. Magnetic resonance neuroimaging characteristically demonstrates diffuse, small focal hyperintense lesions distributed throughout the subcortical white matter and brainstem. Genomic sequencing distinguishes three distinct lineages: the Malaysian M subtype, which predominantly causes acute neurological disease, and the Bangladeshi B and Indian I subtypes, which frequently provoke severe respiratory compromise alongside encephalitis. Pregnancy alters the physiological baseline and clinical trajectory of severe viral infections through stage-specific immunological adaptations rather than generalized immunosuppression. The gestational cycle progresses through three tightly regulated immune phases: an early pro-inflammatory, Th1-skewed environment necessary for blastocyst implantation and spiral artery remodeling; a prolonged mid-gestational anti-inflammatory, tolerogenic milieu mediated by decidual natural killer cells, regulatory T cells, and M2 macrophages to sustain maternal-fetal symbiosis; and a renewed pro-inflammatory surge that triggers parturition. The attenuation of maternal cell-mediated antiviral defenses during the tolerogenic mid-gestational window coincides precisely with the period in which Nipah virus establishes systemic viremia and endothelial invasion. This physiological alignment provides a mechanistic basis for heightened maternal susceptibility to fulminant endothelial damage and central nervous system invasion. Concurrently, normal gestational cardiovascular adaptations, including significant plasma volume expansion, elevated resting cardiac output, and diminished functional residual capacity, drastically reduce cardiopulmonary reserves, thereby lowering the threshold for rapid progression to acute respiratory distress syndrome and hemodynamic collapse. Direct experimental evidence in animal models confirms the biological capacity of Nipah virus to infect reproductive tissues and penetrate the maternal-fetal barrier. In pregnant guinea pig models, intraperitoneal inoculation with 60,000 plaque-forming units produced severe systemic illness and maternal death within four to eight days, with viral shedding recovered from maternal urine, placental structures, and fetal fluids, alongside prominent viral antigen in uterine and ovarian vasculature. More definitive evidence of placental crossing was documented in pregnant cats inoculated subcutaneously with 500 tissue culture infectious doses. Necropsy revealed high concentrations of viral genomic material in the ovaries, uterine horns, placenta, and amniotic fluid, with infectious virus quantified in placental fluid at 126,000 TCID50 per milliliter. Furthermore, viral RNA was identified across all analyzed fetal organs, including the fetal brain, liver, gastrointestinal tract, and thorax, while immunohistochemistry localized viral antigens directly within fetal pulmonary endothelial cells, establishing that transplacental dissemination can induce fetal pulmonary vasculitis and degenerative placentitis. In human medicine, direct clinical observations of Nipah virus during pregnancy remain exceedingly scarce and are derived primarily from outbreak surveillance in Bangladesh between 2007 and 2021. The most comprehensively documented clinical case involved a woman in Faridpur, Bangladesh, who survived laboratory-confirmed acute Nipah virus encephalitis acquired from raw date palm sap in January 2020. Eighteen months following recovery from her initial acute infection, she conceived and subsequently delivered a healthy, full-term infant under rigorous antenatal surveillance. Comprehensive neonatal diagnostic testing revealed undetectable viral RNA via real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and absent anti-Nipah immunoglobulin M antibodies in neonatal specimens. However, high circulating titers of maternal anti-Nipah immunoglobulin G were detected in the infant. This serological finding reflects passive transplacental humoral transfer of protective maternal antibodies rather than vertical viral transmission, as definitive confirmation of congenital infection strictly requires direct isolation of infectious virus or detection of viral RNA and antigen within fetal, placental, or neonatal tissues. Accurate clinical diagnosis during pregnancy requires high epidemiological vigilance due to the overlapping presentation of early viral prodromes with routine obstetric complications. Laboratory confirmation during the acute phase relies primarily on real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction assays performed on nasopharyngeal swabs, throat swabs, urine, blood, or cerebrospinal fluid. In postnatal management, comprehensive neonatal evaluation demands simultaneous polymerase chain reaction testing, immunoglobulin M serology, and serial monitoring of maternal immunoglobulin G decay over time to differentiate benign maternal passive immunity from occult intra-uterine infection. Because no approved vaccines or targeted antiviral therapeutics currently exist for Nipah virus, clinical management focuses on rigorous critical care, strict infection control, and multidisciplinary coordination. Maternal stabilization represents the overriding clinical priority, directing aggressive oxygen supplementation, protective lung mechanical ventilation for respiratory failure, osmotic therapy for intracranial hypertension, hemodynamics stabilization, and anticonvulsant seizure control. The multidisciplinary care team—comprising intensivists, maternal-fetal medicine obstetricians, infectious disease specialists, and neonatologists—must continuously evaluate fetal viability using non-invasive monitoring. In hospital settings, immediate implementation of droplet and contact isolation precautions, strict personal protective equipment protocols, and environmental disinfection with chlorine-based solutions or heat inactivation are essential to prevent nosocomial propagation. Pharmacological interventions remain constrained by scarce safety data and significant fetal risk, leaving experimental countermeasures dependent on compassionate use and emergency regulatory frameworks. Among small-molecule antivirals, favipiravir exhibits documented teratogenic effects in preclinical animal studies, while ribavirin is classified as a potent teratogen contraindicated throughout gestation, and chloroquine has demonstrated no in vivo therapeutic efficacy against Nipah virus in animal challenge models. Conversely, the nucleotide analog remdesivir demonstrated 100 percent survival efficacy in African green monkey challenge models when administered 24 hours post-exposure, with partial therapeutic protection retained at 72 hours. Given extensive human safety data collected during its deployment for maternal COVID-19 without teratogenic signals, remdesivir represents a viable candidate for maternal salvage therapy or post-exposure prophylaxis under strict multidisciplinary oversight. Concurrently, m102.4, a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting the viral G glycoprotein, demonstrates minimal transplacental transfer across the first and second trimesters due to its large immunoglobulin G1 structure, representing the most biologically promising immunotherapeutic candidate for high-risk maternal exposures. The review concludes by outlining critical public health and translational research priorities required to protect pregnant populations from emerging henipavirus threats. Target product profiles for future vaccines and monoclonal antibodies must systematically incorporate pregnant individuals from early preclinical development, mandating formal reproductive toxicology evaluations and pregnancy-specific pharmacokinetic characterizations rather than relying on default exclusion protocols. Regional public health authorities across South and Southeast Asia must integrate explicit pregnancy-focused guidance into seasonal outbreak advisories, particularly warning pregnant women against consuming unpasteurized date palm sap or handling sick livestock. analysis.brief_en: A scientific review published in Frontiers in Public Health on November 15, 2026, examines the challenges of Nipah virus infection during pregnancy. The review highlights that while experimental studies in animals demonstrate the virus's ability to cross the placental barrier and infect fetal organs, confirmed human vertical transmission remains unestablished. Nipah virus, classified by the World Health Organization as an urgent priority pathogen, has a case fatality rate ranging from 40% to 90%. Outbreaks have occurred in Malaysia, Singapore, Bangladesh, and India, with the virus primarily transmitted through contact with infected bats or contaminated date palm sap. The review notes that pregnancy alters the immune environment, creating a tolerogenic phase that may increase maternal susceptibility to the virus. Although the virus can cause severe systemic illness and neurological damage, the study emphasizes the lack of direct clinical evidence for vertical transmission in humans. The findings are based on limited human cases and extensive animal research, underscoring the need for further investigation into the virus's behavior during pregnancy.

news.title: Nipah Virus Transmission in Bangladesh and India Is Overdispersed and Self-Limiting
news.excerpt: A systematic review of Nipah virus outbreaks in Bangladesh and India finds that transmission is self-limiting on average but driven by marked overdispersion.
news.rss_summary_html: A systematic review of Nipah virus outbreaks in Bangladesh and India finds that transmission is self-limiting on average but driven by marked overdispersion.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, November 17, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Nipah Virus Transmission in Bangladesh and India Is Overdispersed and Self-Limiting by November 11, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Nipah Virus Transmission in Bangladesh and India Is Overdispersed and Self-Limiting Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A systematic review and modeling study analyzing Nipah virus transmission dynamics in Bangladesh and India between 2001 and 2026 indicates that viral spread is self-limiting on average but highly overdispersed. Researchers Sol Kim, Vijayalaxmi V. Mogasale, Juan F. Vesga, Hyolim Kang, Laura Skrip, Sung-mok Jung, Ausraful Islam, Akira Endo, W. John Edmunds, and Kaja Abbas evaluated person-to-person transmission of the priority zoonotic pathogen across historical outbreaks. Pooling observations across 67 outbreaks, the authors estimated an overall median reproduction number of 0.43, with a 95 percent credible interval ranging from 0.26 to 0.75, showing that transmission chains typically fail to sustain ongoing community propagation. The investigation addressed distinct transmission patterns that have evolved since early outbreaks were recorded in Malaysia and Singapore, where infections showed limited spread beyond initial spillover events. Since 2001, outbreaks involving direct person-to-person transmission have occurred in Bangladesh and India, driven by the Nipah virus Bangladesh genotype and the Nipah virus India genotype. The study sought to estimate the reproduction number, offspring dispersion, and serial interval governing transmission in both nations over the twenty-five-year period. To establish these epidemiological metrics, the authors conducted a systematic review of outbreak investigations across Bangladesh and India, searching PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and grey literature through 28 February 2026. They gathered case-level offspring counts from 27 sources, comprising 323 cases across 67 outbreaks. These data were used as inputs for a hierarchical Bayesian negative binomial offspring distribution model. Furthermore, the researchers estimated the serial interval by fitting parametric distributions to 137 identified transmission pairs, while performing country-specific analyses and sensitivity analyses to verify the robustness of their findings. In addition to the pooled reproduction number, the analysis yielded a pooled offspring dispersion parameter of 0.04, with a 95 percent credible interval of 0.03 to 0.06, alongside a serial interval of 13.3 days, with a 95 percent confidence interval of 12.8 to 13.8 days. Country-specific estimations revealed that India had a median reproduction number of 0.47 (95 percent credible interval: 0.22 to 0.98) and an offspring dispersion parameter of 0.03 (0.02 to 0.06). Meanwhile, Bangladesh exhibited a median reproduction number of 0.35 (95 percent credible interval: 0.19 to 0.63) and an offspring dispersion parameter of 0.05 (0.03 to 0.09), confirming marked overdispersion in both countries. These statistical metrics demonstrate that while Nipah virus transmission remains self-limiting on average, it is governed by substantial overdispersion. Consequently, a disproportionate share of onward secondary transmission arises from a small fraction of infected cases rather than widespread uniform spread. The authors conclude that this specific epidemiological pattern provides strong empirical backing for focused public health containment measures. analysis.time: The study analyzed Nipah virus transmission dynamics in Bangladesh and India between 2001 and 2026, with the report published on November 11, 2026. The data were collected up to February 28, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on Bangladesh and India, examining outbreaks involving the Nipah virus Bangladesh genotype and Nipah virus India genotype. It included 323 cases across 67 outbreaks.
analysis.event: A systematic review and modeling study evaluated Nipah virus transmission dynamics in Bangladesh and India, revealing that the virus spreads in a self-limiting manner but is highly overdispersed. The findings are based on data from historical outbreaks and are confirmed by the authors.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The pooled reproduction number was estimated at 0.43 (95% credible interval: 0.26 to 0.75), indicating that transmission chains typically fail to sustain ongoing community propagation. The offspring dispersion parameter was 0.04 (95% credible interval: 0.03 to 0.06), and the serial interval was 13.3 days (95% confidence interval: 12.8 to 13.8 days). These metrics confirm marked overdispersion in both countries.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study's findings support focused public health containment measures. The authors conducted a systematic review and used a hierarchical Bayesian negative binomial model to analyze the data, with country-specific analyses and sensitivity checks to ensure robustness. The results are based on empirical data and are not subject to unresolved information.

analysis.brief_en: A study published on November 11, 2026, analyzed Nipah virus transmission dynamics in Bangladesh and India between 2001 and 2026. Researchers evaluated historical outbreaks and found that the virus spreads in a self-limiting pattern, with a pooled reproduction number of 0.43 (95% credible interval: 0.26 to 0.75). This suggests that transmission chains typically fail to sustain ongoing community spread. The study also revealed marked overdispersion, with a pooled offspring dispersion parameter of 0.04 (95% credible interval: 0.03 to 0.06) and a serial interval of 13.3 days (95% confidence interval: 12.8 to 13.8 days). These findings indicate that a small fraction of infected cases drives most secondary transmission. Country-specific analyses showed India had a median reproduction number of 0.47 (95% credible interval: 0.22 to 0.98) and Bangladesh had 0.35 (95% credible interval: 0.19 to 0.63). The authors concluded that these patterns provide empirical support for targeted containment strategies.
